texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 14.06.2024. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 14.06.2024 at about 11.30 a.m., the petitioner was riding a Motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-03-JF-7764 proceeding on Yalachahalli village, Volvo Factory near Bangalore to Kolar NH-75 road, Nandagudi Hobli, Bengaluru, at that time an Auto-Rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-08-5647 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, without following any traffic rules, came at high speed against one way and dashed against the petitioner motorcycle. Due to forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained several grievous injuries. Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to MVJ Hospital, there after shifted to Victoria Hospital and again shifted to MVJ Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food, nourishment and conveyance charges. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 29 years, the petitioner was working as Salesmand and earning Rs.24,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner Abdul Mateen vs Future India Gen Ins Co Ltd on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110525736/ 2 has become permanently disabled and unable to look after the said work. Respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, both the respondents appeared through their counsels and filed their respective written statements. The respondent No.1 in its written statement denied the allegations made in the plaint and submitted that, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-08-5647 and contended that petitioner himself was riding his motorcycle in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Auto-rickshaw. Further, the driver of the Auto-rickshaw was not holding valid and effective driving license, which is in contravention of the policy conditions. Further, the Auto-rickshaw was not having valid permit and fitness certificate as on date of accident and at the time of alleged accident the petitioner was not wearing safety head-gear. The respondent No.2 in its written statement denied the allegations made in the plaint and submitted that, this respondent is the absolute owner of the Auto- rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-08-5647 and is duly insured with the respondent No.1 and policy was inforce as on the date of accident and liability is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. Further both the respondents denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 4. On the basis of above pleadings, following issues are Re-framed: B. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,16,961/- under various heads.
texts.arguments: Hence, at least 01 month is required to recover from the accidental injuries. It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was working as Salesman and earning Rs.24,000/- per month, in support of his income he has not produced any single document. So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,500/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2024 at Rs.16,500/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench. The accident is of the year is 2024. Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- p.m. as per above decision. Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,500/- under this head. 20. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability- The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. Nagaraj B. N in order to substantiate the same, PW.3 has produced documents marked at Ex.P.18 and Ex.P.19. He was sworn that, petitioner has got Disability of 16% to the whole body, but he has not issued the disability certificate. Further, the petitioner also examined the MRD at MVJ Hospital as PW.2, who is Medical Abdul Mateen vs Future India Gen Ins Co Ltd on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110525736/ 6 Record Clerks and deposed and produced only medical documents and his evidence is formal in nature. Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges. The learned counsel for petitioner argued that, accident had happened due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle and as on the date of accident the said offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.2. As such, he argued that, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. The learned counsel for insurance company argued that, as on the date of accident owner of the offending vehicle did not have valid permit to fly the offending vehicle. In support of his argument he relied upon the evidence of RW.1 as well as Ex.R.2 and Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal No. 9322/2022 between Gohar Mohammed Vs. UPSRTC and others. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
